This developmental schedule is an adaptive response to the short breeding seasons characteristic of their temperate and boreal breeding grounds, where early and efficient emergence is critical for maximizing fledging success before seasonal resource availability declines.

As the breeding female approaches the end of the nestling provisioning phase, she attains a characteristic adult body composition. For the Thick-billed warbler, the ultimate wet weight for females is recorded at 22.7 grams [Wwi = 22.7 grams].
